title: The $1 Friction Test
content:
The Insight: Free users provide feedback; paying customers provide validation.

The Tip: If you are struggling to choose between two features for SwiftSell AI, build a 'ghost button' for each that leads to a 'Coming Soon' page with a $1 pre-order or 'Notify Me' option.

The Metric: Ignore the clicks. Only count the people who actually enter their email or click the payment button.

The Goal: $1 is a psychological barrier. Once a user crosses it, they are no longer a spectator; they are a stakeholder. Use this to kill 'zombie ideas' fast.

title: The Paradox of the 'Perfect' Launch
content:
The Insight: If you aren't slightly embarrassed by the first version of your 'Secret Box,' you launched too late.

The Wisdom: In the #BuildInPublic world, your 'cracks' are your features. People don't follow you because you are a finished product; they follow you because they want to see how you handle the pressure of the build.

The Action: Stop polishing the CSS of the vault for a week. Put one raw, unedited voice note of you explaining a problem you’re facing. That raw vulnerability is higher 'value' than a polished PDF.

title: Antigravity vs. Entropy
content:
The Insight: Building a business is a fight against the natural chaos of the world.

The Reflection: In physics, entropy is the inevitable decline into disorder. In business, entropy is 'feature creep,' 'distraction,' and 'burnout.'

The Practice: Every Sunday, look at your project and find one thing to remove. One line of code, one marketing channel that isn't working, or one worry that is taking up headspace.

The Art: Greatness is not what you add; it’s what remains after you’ve stripped away everything that doesn't matter.
